headword: {教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}

definitions.explanation: The 1,026 kanji that Japanese children learn during the six years of elementary school, assigned grade by grade. Materials for beginners and children are often written using only these characters.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}だけで{書|か}かれている。
examples.english: This book is written using only elementary-school kanji.

examples.japanese: {教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}は{学年|がくねん}ごとに{分|わ}けられている。
examples.english: The elementary-school kanji are divided up by grade.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}を{卒業|そつぎょう}するまでに、{子|こ}どもたちは{千|せん}{字|じ}{以上|いじょう}の{教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}を{習|なら}う。
examples.english: By the time they finish elementary school, children have learned over a thousand education kanji.

notes:
Also called {学習漢字|がくしゅうかんじ}. The grade assignment is the {学年別|がくねんべつ}{漢字|かんじ}{配当表|はいとうひょう}, which is why Japanese materials often label a kanji as "grade 3" or "grade 5".

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}を{習|なら}う: to learn the elementary-school kanji
- {教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}だけの{文章|ぶんしょう}: text using only elementary-school kanji
- {学年別|がくねんべつ}{漢字|かんじ}{配当表|はいとうひょう}: the grade-by-grade kanji allocation table

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {常用漢字|じょうようかんじ}: general-use kanji — the wider adult list that includes all the {教育漢字|きょういくかんじ}
- {人名用漢字|じんめいようかんじ}: name kanji — an additional list usable only in personal names
